title: Nocturne AML daily playbook
content:
Quick summary:
- Short daily scratch for experiments on small-ops quant profiles + prompt robustness runs.
- Goal: get a reproducible baseline for 7B-family model (open-7b-v2) using 4-bit quant with per-group scaling (PGS) and a small prefix cache. Check both latency and semantic fidelity.

Today plan / top tasks:
1) Baseline run: open-7b-v2 fp16 @ batch 1, seq 512, no kv cache -> record latency & perplexity. (cmd below)
2) 4-bit PGS quant profile A (LSB2 + outlier clamp) -> run eval_robustness on 200 prompts. Save outputs for diff evaluation.
3) Quick prompt sweep: 10 templated prompts + 5 adversarial rewrites (edgecases). Measure token-level drift and exact-match on answer keys.
4) Check embedding similarity drift for quant vs fp16 (cosine on pooled CLS).
5) If time: try hybrid-kv (cache prefix=64) and measure cold vs warm latency.

Commands / snippets to run (local dev box / rwinf CLI):
- Baseline: python bench/run_infer.py --model open-7b-v2 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 512 --out results/baseline_fp16.json
- Quant A: rwinf quantize --model open-7b-v2 --mode pgs --bits 4 --clamp 0.02 --out models/open-7b-v2-4b-pgsA
- Eval: python bench/eval_prompts.py --model models/open-7b-v2-4b-pgsA --prompts data/prompt-set-200.json --metrics perplexity,emd,exact_match --out results/quantA_eval.json
- Embedding diffs: python bench/emb_compare.py --modelA models/open-7b-v2-fp16 --modelB models/open-7b-v2-4b-pgsA --dataset data/sem-sim-subset.json --metric cosine --out results/emb_diff.json

Prompt set preview (short):
- Q1 (factual): "Who wrote 'The Left Hand of Darkness'? Provide year and publisher."
- Q2 (reasoning): "Summarize the implications of caching KV on streaming token latency for 4b quantized models."
- Q3 (instruction): "Rewrite the following policy paragraph to be clearer for a general audience: <text>"
- Adversarial rewrites: misspellings, truncated context, repeated tokens, nonsensical punctuation.

Experiment notes / heuristics observed so far:
- 4-bit PGS w/ clamp 0.02 seems stable on commonsense QA but degrades on numeric precision tasks (dates, arithmetic). Need to log where exact_match drops below 0.85.
- Warm KV cache critical: warm latency often <20ms/token while cold can be 2-3x depending on kernel. For streaming, startup penalty dominates.
- Batch=1 and small seq -> kernel selection favors row-major matmul path; profiling shows heavy memcpy overhead on our test box (NVIDIA A10x). Consider trying cuBLAS matmul fusion flag.

Metrics to capture (minimum):
- avg wall-token-latency (ms)
- 95p latency
- perplexity (eval set)
- exact_match (where applicable)
- embedding cosine drop (mean & std)
- token overhead (bytes per token after quant)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Does PGS quantization require different layernorm scaling to avoid catastrophic outliers? Quick experiment: add 1e-5 bias correction to layernorm gamma.
- Investigate 'group size' sensitivity: tests for group sizes [32, 64, 128]. Schedule two runs: ASYNC job1/ job2.
- Should we add a calibrated bias-correction step after quant to improve numeric tasks? See notes in linked Confluence page.
- Put an alert (console) if exact_match drops by >10% vs baseline for production rollouts.

Notes to self:
- Save raw logits for a subsample (50 prompts) for posthoc calibration analysis.
- Tag runs with experiment id: nocturne-2026-03-12-A/B/C. Always include git hash in metadata.
- Upload results to shared drive under: /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/quant-results/nocturne-2026-03-12/

Experiment log (quick entries):
- 2026-03-11 10:15: started baseline fp16 run (seq512) -> perf: avg 12.4ms/token, 95p 21ms. Perplexity on eval set 18.7.
- 2026-03-11 13:40: quant A build completed (4-bit PGS clamp0.02). First smoke: functional answers preserved but date errors in 7/200 prompts.
- 2026-03-11 14:05: embedding similarity mean drop 0.024 vs fp16 (std 0.006) on sem-sim-subset.

Notes for writeup / next steps for teammate handoff:
- If handing off, include: git hash, exact command lines, topology (gpus: 1xA10x), dataset versions, and small sample of raw outputs.
- Recommend follow-up run with group-size 64 and clamp 0.01. Also add layernorm bias correction test.

Random scraps / thinking:
- Could we detect semantic drift by measuring downstream classifier probability on original answer vs quantized answer? If classifier confidence drops >0.1, flag.
- Think about integrating a small regression test into Redwood Console that compares a canonical prompt set each deploy. That would catch these exact-match regressions pre-rollout.

End of scratchpad.
